text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here for your 8-month-old son who is having feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. When did you first notice these symptoms, and has he had any vomiting or changes in his bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor

text: Given the X-ray findings and his age, I suspect Hirschsprung disease. Has he ever passed a normal stool, or has he consistently had delayed meconium passage and severe consticence since birth? REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal biopsy makes Hirschsprung disease unlikely, so I am considering functional constipation or another cause of obstruction. Has the baby had a fever, or have you noticed any redness or swelling in the groin area?

text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the rectal biopsy was normal, ruling out Hirschsprung disease, and there are no signs of infection, I need to assess for a mechanical obstruction like an incarcerated hernia or malrotation. speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound makes an incarcerated hernia or malrotation unlikely, so I am now considering a functional issue or a less common anatomical variant.
